name: Design an agent-run media production pipeline: map team roles to tools, encode style as a skill, improve it from feedback
goal: Design an automated media workflow (shown for video editing; same pattern for automated song generation) by listing every human job in the production team, assigning each to a tool with one coordinating agent, writing the creative style into a skill file the agent reads first, and growing that skill from time-stamped human feedback after each run.

source.title: I Fully Automated My Video Editing Using Claude Code (Full Walkthrough)
source.transcript_note: Auto-generated English track, same as Show transcript. Video example is video editing; song-generation mapping is an analogy, not from the video.

prerequisites: A coordinating agent that can run locally, use files and call tools (Claude Code desktop, local mode, working folder set, in the video)
Tools/connectors for each role (video used Parakeet, Hyperframes, Chrome, Tella MCP, Epidemic Sound, FFmpeg)

inputs.name: raw_material
inputs.description: Raw input for the run (raw footage in the video)

inputs.name: style_skill
inputs.description: Instruction file describing preferred style and rules

outputs.name: role_tool_map
outputs.description: Each production job mapped to the tool that does it

outputs.name: updated_skill
outputs.description: Style skill with rules learned from feedback

constraints: The human keeps director jobs: providing the input and giving feedback (human in the loop).
One agent coordinates; it cannot perceive some media directly (it could not hear audio), so add a tool that converts it to readable data (timestamped transcription).
Tools do not know the desired look/sound; that lives in the skill file.
Start with small pieces (a hook) before whole products; feed the full input only once the skill is tuned.
Track cost per run (video measured token use per video).
Mapping to song generation (e.g. composer, sound designer, mixer roles) is an analogy and must be checked against real tools.

steps.action: List every job a human team would do to make the product (video: editor, transcriber, animator, researcher, screen editor, sound designer, finisher).
Assign each job to a tool; make the agent the coordinator/project manager that calls the others, and add a converter for any media the agent cannot perceive.
Set up the agent locally with a working folder and connect each tool/connector, then have the agent save the setup as a skill.
Open a new session and test the skill on a small piece of input, with any extra instructions.
steps.expect: V1 output plus a summary of what the agent did

steps.action: Review the output and give specific, time-stamped feedback (look, sound, pacing, cuts); try several alternatives for one element until one fits.
Tell the agent to save what it learned into the skill, then run the next job in a fresh session with the updated skill.
steps.expect: Skill gains rules (video grew to 36 rules); repeated mistakes stop

steps.action: Once tuned, give the full raw input, let it run unattended, then review and give final notes.
steps.expect: Near-final product needing only a few notes

verification: Every production role has exactly one assigned tool or is marked human
Skill file changes after each feedback round
A fresh session using the updated skill does not repeat an earlier corrected mistake
